items.title: Austria Stays On Budget Track
items.gist: The European Commission says Austria is meeting a key spending limit, but its deficit procedure remains open.
items.summary: The European Commission says Austria is on track to meet a spending limit set under its deficit procedure. The limit concerns the growth of net public spending. The Commission expects this growth to be 2.1 percent in 2026 and 2027. That is just below the recommended limit of 2.2 percent. The procedure is not over, but the Commission says it will take no further steps for now. Austria’s deficit was above the EU’s 3 percent limit in 2024.
items.host_open: Austria has got a little breathing room from Brussels, though the paperwork is not finished. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Linz Power Outage Investigated
items.gist: Police suspect deliberate damage after a fault left thousands of homes without power.
items.summary: A power outage affected about 20,000 households in Linz on Monday morning. The outage began after a fault at a substation in the Kleinmünchen area. Police say their investigation suggests the fault may have been caused deliberately. They are investigating suspected serious property damage. The cause has not been finally established, and no suspect has been named. The case matters because it raises questions about the security of local power infrastructure.
items.host_open: A short power cut can affect a lot of people at once. How does the investigation make you feel?

items.title: Ukraine Attack Kills Libyan Soldiers
items.gist: Two Libyan soldiers died after Ukrainian attacks on Russian ships near Benghazi, according to eastern Libyan authorities.
items.summary: Two Libyan soldiers have died from injuries after Ukrainian attacks on two Russian ships near Libya. The deaths were announced by authorities in eastern Libya. The attacks took place near the port of Benghazi. France’s foreign minister defended Ukraine’s actions as self-defence against Russia’s invasion. The Libyan authorities described the attacks as aggression. The reports add a new dimension to the war, but details of the attack have not been independently confirmed in the report.
items.host_open: Two soldiers have died after an attack near Benghazi. How do you feel about this widening risk to people outside Ukraine?

items.title: Iran Reports Tanker Explosions
items.gist: Iran says two ships hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, but the claim could not be independently checked.
items.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says two oil tankers struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The report says the claim could not initially be verified independently. Iran’s navy warned shipping companies against using routes it had not approved. The US military has been escorting civilian ships to help restore oil and gas trade. Talks between Tehran and Washington have not produced a breakthrough. The strait is an important route for energy shipments, so any threat to shipping could matter internationally.
items.host_open: Reports of mines in a busy shipping lane raise serious safety concerns. How does that news make you feel?

items.title: Eurostar Trains Hit By Strike
items.gist: Unexpected industrial action disrupted trains between France and Britain on Wednesday.
items.summary: Eurostar said an unexpected strike disrupted train services between France and Britain on Wednesday. The company did not give details about the strike. It asked unions to continue talks directly with management. An AFP report cited company sources who said wage negotiations were under way. The same sources said staff were unhappy about a planned farewell event for a former chief executive. Passengers faced cancellations in both directions through the Channel Tunnel.
items.host_open: A strike has disrupted one of Europe’s key rail links. Did that surprise you?

items.title: A1 Austria Plans 430 Job Cuts
items.gist: The telecom company plans a net reduction of 430 positions in Austria in 2027 as part of a cost-saving drive.
items.summary: A1 Austria plans to reduce its workforce by a net 430 jobs in 2027. The plan includes 500 departures and 70 new jobs in future-focused areas. The company currently employs just under 6,000 people in Austria. A1 says it wants to cut costs by 300 million euros by 2030. About 100 million euros of the planned savings would come from staff costs. The company also says it will continue investing in fibre, mobile networks and IT projects.
items.host_open: A1 plans to cut more jobs while still investing in its network. How does that balance look to you?

items.title: New Test Can Detect GHB Later
items.gist: A laboratory in Austria is using a method that can detect the drug GHB in blood for up to two days.
items.summary: A new method can detect GHB in blood for up to two days after it is taken. GHB is a drug often linked to so-called knockout drops. A laboratory in Seibersdorf is among the few places already using the method. The laboratory examines samples in cases referred by clinics, police or courts. Until now, GHB was usually detectable in the body for only six to twelve hours. The longer window may help investigators, although many suspected cases still have no confirmed trace of the drug.
items.host_open: A longer testing window could make evidence easier to find. How does that sound to you?

items.title: Paris Uses Cards To Challenge Sexism
items.gist: Paris is distributing a card game in schools and youth centres to help teenagers recognise misogynistic ideas online.
items.summary: Paris has begun distributing a card game called Mascuradar. The game is intended to help young people recognise misogynistic statements and harmful ideas about masculinity online. It is aimed at boys aged about twelve and older. Schools, youth centres and local town halls are among the first places to receive the cards. The project was developed by the group En avant toutes and Paris’s observatory on violence against women. The city plans to make the cards available in all its secondary schools next year.
items.host_open: Paris is using a card game to start a serious conversation with teenagers. Would that approach surprise you?
